The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature for the shop's account pages ran a calculation that fails when a shopper has no purchases in the current month, likely shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 20m 12s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 36.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 7,773.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #559 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Incident: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 04:20 UTC, not back to normal by 04:40:12 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 8 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:59:34 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:26:20 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 04:40:12 UTC - PR #559, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 04:20 UTC and was not back to normal by 04:40:12 UTC, at least 20 minutes 12 seconds later. 19.8% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 36.5% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 7,773.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly-spending feature for the shop's account pages ran a calculation that fails when a shopper has no purchases in the current month, likely shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #559, for a person to review and merge. Account page requests could keep failing with ZeroDivisionError while monthly-spend-feature evaluates on, and switching the flag off might again leave some minutes evaluating on.

Impact
at least 20m 12s - since onset, still not back to normal
36.5% - peak error rate
4,986 - requests failed
1.0% to 19.8% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 2.5%)
at least 7,773.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the shopper's month-to-date total by the number of purchases in the current month and has no case for when there are none. A shopper who has bought before but not this month brings that number to 0, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and `serve_account_page` catches it and returns a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged a raised account page error rate.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 43 occurrences in 47 minutes, 03:51–04:37; # was 0.50% to 36.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 04:24. After Argus first acted, logged in 04:27–04:33,04:35–04:37
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 18 occurrences in 18 minutes, 04:20–04:37. After Argus first acted, logged in 04:28,04:31,04:37
why 1 Those requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appears in the logs at the onset and not in the earlier minutes read.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The failing code ran because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at 04:20:05 UTC. From that minute most flag evaluations returned on. After the flag was switched off at 04:26:49 UTC, the error was logged only in the minutes when evaluations still returned on.
  Evidence:
    P1 04:20:05 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off # / on # - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 7 minutes, 04:20–04:26; # was 27 to 36, typically 27, highest at 04:26; # was 164 to 173, typically 164, highest at 04:20
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 8 occurrences in 17 minutes, 04:21–04:37. After Argus first acted, logged in 04:28,04:31,04:37
    G5309
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 04:21; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change. A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T7
      T8
      T9
why 3 When the flag is on, the code divides by the number of the shopper's purchases in the current month and does not handle the case where there are none.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that served the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (AI-2)
- From its first minute, the flag returned on for most evaluations. No smaller staged step was seen. (AI-3, AI-4)
- ErrorRateSustained on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 04:20:05 UTC. Account page requests then began failing with a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 35%. No deployment was involved. | 0.93 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 04:20:05 UTC. This enabled the spend summary path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails about 30% of account page requests. No code or config changed, and no deployment exists. Argus switched the flag off at 04:25:17 UTC, but later minutes still show the flag evaluating on and the errors returning. Some evaluations kept serving the on value after the off toggle, so the flag state looks inconsistent. | 0.90 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 04:26:58 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 04:40:11 | Proposed a fix: PR #559 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:20 UTC. ErrorRateSustained fired at 04:25:58 UTC, 5 minutes 58 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above 2.5% averaged over 10m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #559 | open
AI-2 | Require a passing run of io-shop's tests with a feature flag on before that flag can be switched on in production. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Roll out io-shop feature flags in staged steps, starting with a small share of evaluations. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Halt a flag rollout step automatically when the account page error rate rises during it. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link ErrorRateSustained on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that it pages a person. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop that every minute's evaluations log monthly-spend-feature=off, with no monthly-spend-feature=on line, and that no account page request fails with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Find out whether the switch-off at 04:26:49 UTC reached every io-shop flag evaluation. After it, the service still logged minutes in which evaluations returned on (04:28, 04:31 and 04:37 UTC), with the ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes (04:28, 04:31 and 04:37 UTC). If the switch-off did reach every evaluation, find out why the service stayed at the incident's level. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 46 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 14 minutes 13 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #559.
What went wrong
- The alert came 3 minutes 28 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
- The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and put monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet the logs after the switch-off showed evaluations still returning on in the same minutes the ZeroDivisionError came, so the flag was left on with the failing code in use.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides account.total_this_month_cents by the number of purchases where in_current_month is true. It does not handle the case where there are none. A shopper who has bought before but not this month brings that number to 0, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. render_spend_summary sends a request to this function when use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false. serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches the exception at its boundary and returns a failed page. That is how turning on monthly-spend-feature showed up as account page failures. Turning the flag off hides the bug but leaves it in place.

The change: when no purchases fall in the current month, the function now returns 0, because the shopper's spend this month really is zero. This is a correct figure, not a swallowed error. The empty case now has a defined answer, and any other failure still reaches the caller. The lifetime average is unchanged, and so is the existing test that expects a shopper with no history at all to raise on the flag-off path. Nothing in account_page.py changes: it still gets an int either way.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new cases. One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month on an account that has past purchases but none this month and asserts 0. Against the old code that call raises ZeroDivisionError. The other checks the same account through render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True.

Not covered here: the investigation also reports flag evaluations still returning on after the off toggle. Nothing in this repository evaluates the flag. render_spend_summary and serve_account_page take the decision as an argument. With this fix, an on evaluation no longer crashes for these shoppers, whatever the flag's state.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not open their account pages. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. The trouble started when a new monthly-spending feature was switched on for the account pages. The feature runs a calculation that fails for any shopper with no purchases in the current month, so their account pages would not load. The shoppers affected were likely those who have bought from the shop before but not this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no one on call was pulled in to respond. Argus switched the new feature back off, but that did not help, so Argus turned it back on. Argus has also written a proposed fix. It is still a draft and has not yet been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.
